title: Interface Delamination in Thin-Film Si Modules

key_findings.detail:
**Linear-shape delamination:**
- Grows uniformly from scribe lines (P1, P2, P3) across the full module width
- Occurs at or near the P1, P2, P3 scribing areas where the glass/TCO and TCO/thin-film Si interfaces are exposed
- Forms during the **first PID stress cycle**; once formed, it is **irreversible**
- Visible in outdoor field modules after 5 years of operation, concentrated near the bottom Al frame

**Spot-shape delamination:**
- Circular spots, approximately **200 µm diameter**
- Located at the TCO/thin-film Si interface within the cell area
- Appear predominantly after the **second negative voltage stress cycle** (following a +1000 V recovery cycle)
- Larger number of spots correlates directly with larger Pmax loss
- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=4|Shioda et al. (2017), p.4]]

Na⁺ ions from glass reach the interface between FTO and a-Si:H directly (no encapsulant barrier):

- Na⁺ reacts chemically with the TCO/a-Si:H interface, weakening interfacial adhesion
- The electrochemical reaction creates gas or reaction products at the interface, causing physical separation
- OH⁻ ions generated at the surface also contribute to hydrolytic attack of the interface
- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=3|Shioda et al. (2017), p.3]]

A critical diagnostic distinguisher from c-Si PID:

- **Shunt resistance (Rsh) does NOT decrease** in thin-film Si PID
- This absence of shunting confirms delamination (loss of electrical contact) rather than shunt formation as the dominant failure
- The equivalent circuit changes as delaminated areas become inactive rather than shunted
- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=2|Shioda et al. (2017), p.2]]

key_findings.claim: Degradation Rate: Before and After Recovery Cycle
key_findings.detail:
A characteristic feature of thin-film Si PID is catastrophic acceleration after a recovery/re-stress cycle:

- **First −1000 V stress (300 h):** Gradual degradation to ~60% Pmax
- **+1000 V recovery:** Complete recovery of all electrical parameters
- **Second −1000 V stress:** Catastrophic degradation — equivalent damage in **36 hours** vs. 250+ hours in first cycle
- Each cycle nucleates additional delamination sites; once linear delamination forms, complete recovery is impossible
- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=5|Shioda et al. (2017), p.5]]

Outdoor modules aged 5 years showed:
- Linear delamination concentrated near the bottom Al frame (primary moisture/Na ingress point)
- Delamination at junction box cutouts (secondary entry path)
- Spot-shaped delamination matching laboratory accelerated test morphologies
- [[papers/IOP-48-3326-2-s2.0-85017152617-2017-J-Potential-induced degradation of thin-film Si photovoltaic modules.pdf#page=6|Shioda et al. (2017), p.6]]
